newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown won't propose BOE independence today.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown won't propose BOE independence today.

text.p: Gordon Brown, finance spokesman for Britain's opposition Labour party, said he would not propose operational independence for the Bank of England in a speech he will deliver at 1800 GMT on Wednesday.
He told BBC radio he wanted a broadening of the economic expertise available to the Bank.

"I'm not proposing operational independence for the Bank of England in my speech this evening. What I am saying is that we need an interest rate decision-making process that is free from short-term considerations."
Decisions on monetary policy would remain with the Chancellor, Brown said.
"But we will look at these things as we progress," he added.

"First of all we've got to extend the economic expertise of the monetary policy committee. Secondly, we've got to broaden the economic advice that is available to the Treasury itself -- that's why I propose a Council of Economic Advisers."
Brown said he would then look at the track record of the Bank of England and how the monetary policy committee worked.
Monetary policy should be freed from political manipulation and any suspicion that it was being used for party-political ends.
Pressed on whether his ultimate goal was independence for the Bank, Brown said:

"You don't jump to transferring decision-making power until you have looked at both whether you've got the structure properly in place and whether the economic expertise is working effectively and you've got a track record."
"I will look at the situation after we evaluate these two things."

The shadow chancellor said the changes he was proposing were some of the biggest since the 1940s and would help Britain to escape from the "stop-go" economic policies that had long bedevilled the country.
